sections.content: How many people are "publicans and managers of licensed premises"?

38,100 people

were counted on the census as "publicans and managers of licensed premises" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Publicans and managers of licensed premises organise and direct the activities and resources of public houses (non-residential and residential) and bar and catering facilities at non-residential clubs.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "publicans and managers of licensed premises" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "publicans and managers of licensed premises", 12.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "publicans and managers of licensed premises" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "publicans and managers of licensed premises" included:

  • biological scientists
  • chartered surveyors
  • estimators, valuers and assessors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "publicans and managers of licensed premises" there were a similar number of men and women (54.4% compared with 45.6%).

This means "publicans and managers of licensed premises" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 54.4% and women made up 45.6% of "publicans and managers of licensed premises"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "publicans and managers of licensed premises" included:

  • design occupations (other)
  • leisure and travel service occupations (other)
  • shelf fillers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "publicans and managers of licensed premises" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "publicans and managers of licensed premises" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "publicans and managers of licensed premises", 12.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (73.5% compared with 26.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (62.2%) than self-employed (37.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
